title: Trump: 12 Russia GRU agents indicted for hacking and 2016 election interference
description_short: Trump: 12 Russia GRU agents indicted for hacking and 2016 election interference
description_medium: On July 13, 2018, Deputy Attorney General Rod Rosenstein announced indictments against 12 officers of Russia’s GRU. Prosecutors accused them of hacking Democratic and campaign-related systems during the 2016 election; an indictment is an allegation, not a conviction. The defendants were charged, not convicted, in the announcement.
description_long: Deputy Attorney General Rod Rosenstein announced on July 13, 2018, that a federal grand jury had indicted 12 members of Russia’s military intelligence agency, the GRU. Special Counsel Robert Mueller’s team charged them with conspiring to hack computers belonging to Americans and U.S. organizations connected to the 2016 election. The indictment described alleged intrusions into Democratic Party systems and the theft and release of campaign materials. The announcement attributed the activity to Russian military intelligence through a formal criminal charging document. It did not mean the defendants had appeared in U.S. court or been convicted; the charges were prosecutors’ allegations. The event occurred while Trump was president and Russian interference remained politically central. The indictment set out those charges but did not resolve every question about election influence or contacts with U.S. campaigns themselves.
